title: AI-proposed product tax codes with confidence scores, reviewed by a person
problem: Mapping thousands of products to the right tax code by hand is slow and inconsistent, and wrong mappings produce wrong tax that is hard to defend in an audit.
approach: A model proposes a tax code with a confidence score; Vertex, Thomson Reuters, Sovos and Avalara offer this; Dell trained small models.
Vertex's CEO says categorisation fell from over a minute and a half to seconds per product (vendor-published).
A person confirms or overrides each suggested code; low-confidence suggestions are reviewed or sent back for more product detail.
who: Vertex, Thomson Reuters, Sovos, Avalara, Dell

title: Agent-prepared sales tax and VAT returns, filed only after human approval
problem: US sales tax reporting spans more than 19,000 jurisdictions, and 71% of surveyed indirect tax teams have not fully automated a single workflow end to end.
approach: Agents ingest transaction data, validate it, map it to returns and present them for approval; Thomson Reuters, Avalara and Deloitte describe this.
Thomson Reuters states routine reporting time falls by up to 65% and compliance cycles from 30 days to 11 (vendor-published).
Final review and approval come before filing, and agents notify a person for novel situations.

title: AI validation and routing of exemption certificates as they arrive
problem: Exemption and resale certificates are among the most manual areas of compliance, and certificate errors can lead to audit exposure and penalties.
approach: Avalara says its Exemption Certificate Management ingests, classifies, validates and routes certificates with document processing, spots missing fields and flags errors.
Avalara says AI review is faster and more accurate than manual review; no figure is published (vendor-published).
Flagged or failed certificates route to a person; Avalara says agents ask a human for novel situations.

title: Re-checking every exemption certificate already on file
problem: Certificates are collected, stored and checked by hand, so invalid or expired certificates stay undiscovered until an audit.
approach: Document intelligence extracts and validates every certificate on file; Avalara describes agents that cross-check certificates against authoritative registries.
Numeral reports that 30% to 40% of certificates moved onto its platform fail validation (vendor-published).
The source does not describe the review step for certificates; Avalara says human approval checkpoints exist across its agent platform.

title: Grounded taxability and regulatory Q&A assistant inside the tax platform
problem: Staff spend time finding taxability answers across jurisdictions, and a general chatbot can be confidently wrong, as in one Avalara example of a wrong local rate.
approach: Platform assistants answer from a curated knowledge base: Sovos's Ask Sovi, Avalara Aviator and Vertex Copilot.
A beta customer at Singer Equipment Company says Aviator surfaces considerations she might have missed; no figures published (vendor-published).
The user decides what to do with an answer; Sovos plans guided, human-approved actions.
who: Sovos, Avalara, Vertex, Singer Equipment Company

title: VAT place-of-supply assistant grounded in law, answers verified by a tax adviser
problem: Clients describe VAT cases in free-text emails, and advisers must determine the place of supply and justify it from statute, where errors carry significant financial consequences.
approach: A language model retrieves passages of Austrian and EU VAT law and returns a place-of-supply decision citing its legal sources.
On textbook cases retrieval scored 93.24% against 68.92% for the plain model; on 20 real inquiries it got 16 right (independent research).
A tax adviser checks every cited paragraph and approves the analysis before it reaches the client.

title: Plain-language drafting of tax-engine rules, simulated on past transactions first
problem: Configuring custom tax rules in a tax engine needs specialist knowledge of the product and the law, and changes can conflict with other rules.
approach: Avalara's agent drafts a rule from a plain-language request, simulates it on past transactions and flags conflicts; Vertex showed similar plain-language configuration.
Avalara claims Aviator turns days of manual work into minutes of oversight (vendor-published).
The customer reviews and approves the drafted rule before the agent activates it.

title: E-invoice rejection diagnosis, with corrections made after a user approves
problem: Under clearance e-invoicing an invoice has no legal force until the authority accepts it, so a wrong VAT ID or malformed schema means rejection and stalled goods and payment.
approach: Sovos's Sovi AI diagnoses root causes of compliance errors, proposes fixes and executes them once a user approves, logging each action.
Thomson Reuters demonstrated AI exception handling in ONESOURCE; Sovos reports a 1.6% rejection rate in French production, not credited to AI (vendor-published).
A user approves each proposed correction before it executes, and tax reviews recurring root causes.

title: Continuous regulatory-change monitoring with alerts linked to primary sources
problem: Monitoring often relies on one person watching a few countries and forwarded newsletters, so rule changes frequently surface only at filing time.
approach: Fonoa Knowledge monitors centrally, filtered to the company's jurisdictions, with each alert linked to the primary source and a confidence score.
Sovos assesses how rule changes affect each customer's configuration; Avalara's research agents summarise primary sources with citations. No outcome figures are published.
Fonoa says deciding whether a change applies to the business may need a human's deterministic application.

title: AI extraction of invoice and expense data for VAT recovery and e-invoicing
problem: Fragmented travel, expense and payables data must be cleansed and enriched before eligible input VAT can be recovered, and e-invoicing regimes need accurate onboarding and data extraction.
approach: Blue dot's platform extracts, cleanses and validates invoice and expense data; Sovos bought it in September 2026 and plans to embed it.
Vertex bought AI e-invoicing start-up Brinta in Q1 2026; Sovos says Blue dot has shown accuracy above 98% (vendor-published).
The sources do not describe the human review step.

title: Pre-filing anomaly detection and exception triage across invoice and tax data
problem: Misapplied rates, address mismatches and unusual swings in tax amounts need catching before filing, but manual review samples only a small share of transactions.
approach: Models flag outliers in tax data before filing and route exceptions to reviewers; Thomson Reuters, Sovos and Fonoa describe this.
Thomson Reuters says some indirect tax teams use AI to triage invoice exceptions; no outcome figures are published (vendor-published).
Flagged items go to review, and a tax manager verifies flags against known rules.

title: Idea: validate and repair tax-relevant master and transaction data at entry
problem: This is an idea: most indirect-tax errors start upstream in missing fields and inconsistent configuration, and only 23% of surveyed multinationals say their ERP is fit for purpose.
approach: Practitioners discuss agents near master-data setup and payables flows that extract, enrich and validate data as transactions occur, not at return time.
In KPMG's survey about 49% said improving data quality will be their primary AI use case, an intention (independent survey).
AI surfaces results for human review where judgment is required, and the tax team approves rule changes.

title: Nexus monitoring, nexus questions and registration agents
problem: Companies cross economic-nexus thresholds or start selling into new countries without registering in time, and registration is paper-heavy and multi-authority.
approach: Avalara registration agents prepare and file registration documents and track them to signed storage; Numeral supports nexus monitoring and registrations.
Numeral states customers can cut time on filings and registrations by up to 80% (vendor-published).
Avalara states human review checkpoints at every stage, and Deloitte's agent flags patterns for tax professionals to consider.

title: Intake, data extraction and routing of tax-authority notices
problem: Tax-authority notices arrive in many forms and jurisdictions and must be received, classified, routed and tracked to deadlines.
approach: Avalara describes notice-management agents that automate receipt, classification, routing and tracking of notices across jurisdictions.
Seminar attendees described using image-to-text AI to pull structured data out of state tax notices. No outcome figures are published.
Avalara states review and approval checkpoints at every stage; notice-specific checkpoints are not described.

title: Audit-ready decision records for AI-assisted tax determinations, overrides and filings
problem: In one survey, 57.4% of indirect tax leaders would not be confident defending AI-assisted decisions to a tax authority, and few run formal documented sign-off.
approach: Log each AI-assisted determination, override and approval with rule version, inputs, rationale and reviewer; Fonoa, Thomson Reuters, Sovos and Avalara describe this.
Fonoa's survey found organisations with formal human-in-the-loop governance were more than twice as likely to be confident (vendor-published).
A named human owns each AI-supported decision; tax professionals answer the authority while agents prepare documentation.
who: Fonoa, Deloitte, Thomson Reuters, Sovos, Avalara

title: Tax engines callable by customers' own AI agents through standard protocols
problem: Tax calculation, classification, registration and filing sit inside tax applications, but compliance work may now start in an ERP, a finance system or an AI agent.
approach: Avalara described MCP servers letting customers' agents validate taxes and start registrations; Sovos is developing a governed gateway; Vertex builds ERP agents.
Avalara says its Versori unit builds connectors in days rather than months (vendor-published).
Avalara says agents notify a human for novel situations and decisions that affect the compliance footprint.

title: Tax calculation and holiday rules when an AI agent checks out
problem: When an AI agent completes a purchase there may be no human at checkout, so who must collect tax is unclear, and tax holidays need exact timing and category rules.
approach: Keep tax calculation in the merchant's existing tax engine, called from the agent's checkout; the Sales Tax Institute says Shopify did this.
Make holiday rules machine-readable and give agents correct catalogue data; no outcome figures are published (independent).
Controls move to the tax engine and data, and tax and e-commerce teams confirm configuration before peak events.

title: Finance agents that embed VAT and e-invoicing rules in payables and invoicing
problem: Companies bolting separate finance and tax applications onto ERPs face integration and governance burdens, while authorities require real-time clearance against local rules.
approach: Sovos bought Flowie on 1 October 2026; its agents run payables, procure-to-pay and invoicing on an ERP using Sovos's regulatory data.
Sovos cites an EY figure of up to 40% for agentic finance implementations; the EY source was not opened (vendor-published).
Human checkpoints are not described in the release.

title: AI-enabled managed sales tax and VAT compliance delivered as a service
problem: Software, distribution and manufacturing companies face changing multi-state and multi-country tax obligations and want them handled without adding manual work.
approach: Providers such as Numeral run the lifecycle (nexus, registration, filing, certificates) on an AI-native platform covering VAT/GST in more than 90 countries.
Numeral reports transaction volume growth of 327% year over year and Taxually reports client growth of almost 40% (vendor-published).
Complex issues go to tax experts at the provider.

title: General-purpose AI for first-pass analysis and month-end summaries in an approved workspace
problem: An in-house indirect tax manager owns compliance in several countries, and 60.8% of surveyed organisations rely mainly on individuals using public AI tools without governance.
approach: A Plusgrade job posting says AI handles first-pass recurring data analysis and month-end tax summaries so the manager focuses on judgment (self-reported).
The recommendation is to provide approved, grounded tools with logging and a use policy; no outcome figures are published.
The Tax Manager owns the final call, and a reviewer checks AI research output against primary sources.

title: Idea: ongoing indirect-tax exposure, accrual and scenario analysis by agents
problem: This is an idea: indirect-tax teams answer ad hoc questions about supply-chain changes and pricing, and book conservative accruals because of data gaps.
approach: Practitioners suggest agents run ongoing scenario analysis, give a view of exposures that may reduce over-accruals, and flag transactions creating unmanaged exposure.
Thomson Reuters Institute adds forecasting VAT cash flows and quantifying audit exposure by country, product and customer segment.
Agents provide structured input for tax professionals to consider.

title: Idea: a rule engine checks each step of AI-agent VAT determination
problem: This is an idea: model agents that classify, rate and apply reverse charge can fail silently, and in one study 20-30% of real-world VAT analyses were wrong.
approach: Split VAT determination into auditable steps, let model agents handle language and lookup, and check every step against a deterministic rule engine.
In a preprint pilot on synthetic cases, a tuned single agent scored 0.755 accuracy and the best orchestrated set-up 0.830 (independent research).
A tax expert approves outputs the rule engine cannot confirm, and rule-set changes are reviewed.
